notes.title: [Major Update] Release 1.1.1
notes.content: [p]Heyho![/p][p][/p][p]We are finally done with the beta - after a last-minute struggle of me getting the build online because I activated the steam authenticator, blocking my ability to set a build live... Well, it is now done, let's focus on the update![/p][p]There is a lot that's new in this update, most of which I had already announced in my previous post where I talked about the road post 1.0. Here I will give a quick run-down on what's new:[/p][h3]1.) The new Maid Ending[/h3][p]This new complex of content is not just a quick bad end - it comes with a complete new mini section of playable content before the Festival. Agree to join the Festival by working as Arwin's Full-Time Maid for 3 days to trigger [b]new Maid Job[/b] scenes and use the opportunity of infiltrating your enemy to gain new advantages in the Festival event.[/p][p]However... Can Aura still fight against her "Master" after going through three days of maid training?! The answer depends on the choices Aura makes during her time as Arwin's maid and how much she is willing to "perform" as an obedient maid to get future advantages.[/p][p]The new maid ending can be triggered both through the Full-Time Maid job and by simply losing to Arwin at the Festival. The epilogue scenes contain some variations to reflect the circumstances.[/p][h3]2.) Alternate Costumes for Earth Aura[/h3][p]When advancing the corruption route, you now have the choice between [b]two costumes for each new clothing corruption phase[/b].[/p][p]They both require quite a bit of Exhibitionism to unlock but also give extra Exhibitionism in their respective corruption scenes, giving th. The new costumes are fully reflected in all other visual content.[/p][h3]3.) Alternate game modes (NG-)[/h3][p]The Clear Room has been expanded with new choices for using your Score: [b]New Game Minus[/b]. For New Game Minus, you have to invest Score and in return you an extra Score %. Besides simple modifiers, there are two NG- options that add new game modes:[/p][list][*][p]Ironman Mode - I think this kind of gameplay mode is well known, so I won't have to explain further.[/p][/*][*][p]Hidden Alicia Mode - In this mode, the mental world segment is no longer player controlled. Alicia will automatically apply mental changes and you will have no idea what she just did. For those who fully want to immerse in the role of Aura instead of the dual character setup.[/p][/*][/list][h3]4.) Community Translation Support[/h3][p]We have greatly overhauled the base rules of RPGMaker text processing in order to integrate a [b]translation engine[/b].[/p][p]Please note, we only added the technical support for adding translations! The game hasn't been suddenly translated into different languages, but we do have amazing community members who have started working on community translations. If you are interested in contributing, join the Discord![/p][h3]5.) General Polish Work[/h3][p]Well, this one isn't so clear-cut as the others as it's a bunch of little work here and there that we have done to improve the reactivity, visuals, and quality of life of the game. It's not an earth-shattering amount so I'm not sure how visible it is to most players.[/p][p]Various NPCs in the Trademond area (such as Arwin's maids or the miners) now execute pixel animations to make them more alive. Aura has improved dialogue reactivity (in particular if the player has reached Chapter 3), there are new NPCs you can find in-town (Doll Aura starts moving around eventually!), Charlotte received a new artwork after she becomes Lady Charlotte, and so on and so forth.[/p][p]I'm just going to refer to the masssive changelog below for the interested readers. I tried to compress the changelog to make it a bit more readable than just concatinating all the prerelease changelogs.[/p][p]Have fun with the update![/p]

notes.title: Release 1.0.7
notes.content:
Heyho!

Maintenance patch and one significant balancing change: On Explorer and Story mode purification effects had their effects doubled again - that is, Blessed Water and co now reduce x4 as much corruption compared to the Normal mode.

The reason for this is the same reason as the doubling effect was introduced initially: If a player wanted to take his time (a design goal for Explorer and easier) and also not continue down on the corruption route, this would cause corruption to accumulate. While Soul-Break is disabled on these difficulty modes, effects such as the stat debuffs remain.

A purification factor of 4 means that through buying the 3 x Blessed Water restock every 20 days (=10 Corruption from 20 days, and =-12 Corruption from the Blessed Water), you can effectively reduce the time-based corruption gain to 0 on these difficulty modes given sufficient money to buy Blessed Water.

Since Explorer is not supposed to trivialize the game and only soften up the time-aspect, the gold increase of Blessed Water should prevent a true "infinite" corruption reduction. On story mode where trivialization is okay, the massive amounts of gold you get should allow you to continously fuel the corruption reduction if so desired.

It's a bit of a risky balancing change due to the risk of overtrivializing Explorer Mode since the corruption reduction can also be used to get a lot free Star Knightess usages, but based on my data it should be fine, so I want to give it a try.

notes.title: [Devlog] The road past 1.0
notes.content:
Heyho!

It's already been nearly two months since the game's 1.0 release, sheesh, time flies by fast.

[h1]Post-1.0 Roadmap[/h1]

Those who have been following the game's development on other social media sites, probably already know on my post-release plans. In this post I want to summarize the main important points for the Steam audience including a roadmap of future updates and a sneak-peak on what we have been up to over the past month (besides bugfixing).

For the 1.0 release I largely focused on producing a coherent, complete game within the scope of my available resources in terms of budget and development time. As such, I focused on features that would ultimately always serve the purpose of bringing the player closer towards the Corruption Ending or the Victory Ending.

Since our resources are limited, my artist can only produce art so fast, that of course means focusing on certain aspects, while having to cut out other nice-to-have options. The focus of the post 1.0 development (or "2.0 development") is to focus on those aspects that I had to cut. I based this development approach a bit on how Larian Games developed the games Divinity: Original Sin 1/2. In a similar way, you can think of the end of the development road of 2.0 to be a sort of Enhanced version.

Don't expect a lot of new content in terms of new main storylines. The main story is definitely finished. The focus of 2.0 will be on:
[list]
[*] More choices - Different costume choices.
[*] More reactivity - Better reflection of Aura's current corruption status, more ending variations.
[*] More replayability - New game modes.
[*] Longer lewd event chains - Various characters will receive more events for their event chain so you aren't forced to pick ones you don't like to further Aura's corruption and can instead focus on the ones you do like.
[/list]

Besides working on Star Knightess Aura, I am also currently in the process of starting up my next game. The plan is to work 50% on SKA and 50% on that new game. That in particular allows my artist (I will be using different artists for the different games) to produce content at a faster pace than I expand the game. This would allow us to increase the art density in the existing game.

Currently I am working on the first post-1.0 major update (Version 1.1 "Maid Bad End") and expect that it will need about 3-4 months of work (with the first one done in March). Due to the 50% time investment, I expect it to finish in about 4-6 months, so about August - October.

For the roadmap over roughly the next two years, I have roughly planned to put the following updates:
[list]
[*] 1.1 "Maid Bad End"
[*] 1.2 "Roland Bad End"
[*] 1.3 "Hermann & Other Repeatables"
[*] 1.4 "Companions"
[/list]

I have focused the planning around the extra lewd chain event expansions, but that doesn't mean they are the only thing that will be worked on for them. To give a better idea, I would like to talk for the rest of this post on the work we have done in March for the 1.1 update.

[h1]Major Update 1.1.0 - Maid Bad End[/h1]

As the name suggests. the main focus on the update is adding an extra option for going to the Festival. 

[h2]Full-Time Maid Job[/h2]

in this case by asking Arwin for a full-time job opportunity so you can join the Festival as a working maid. The event is planned to take 3 full days of working as his maid until you can then join the Festival. Last month, I implemented the first day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41560265/e1f35bce1f331bb33c8bb14f447a83bf93da02d4.png[/img]

The plan is that depending on your choices during those three days you can make the Festival event easier at the risk of triggering the titular bad end if you go too far in pretending to be a good maid.

[h2]Alternate Earth Costumes[/h2]

We added three alternate costumes for Earth Aura that Alicia can pick from when she performs the Clothing Mental Change.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41560265/a9613f6d24fd4e3f776d8645dc0a379c3908349f.png[/img]

They have minimal impact on the gameplay in form of trading in more Corruption and gaining secondary stats in exchange. However, to unlock them you will need to pass some Exhib checks.

[h2]New Game Minus[/h2]

New Game Plus (NG+) bonuses allow you to make your life easier in exchange for Score. New Game Minus (NG-) is the opposite concept of that: Invest Score to gain modifiers that make Aura's life more difficult but gain extra multipliers for the score evaluation in return.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41560265/9b4139614189dffca72e7b54bce5231ace69a51a.png[/img]

The NG- modifiers can make Aura initially weaker or add an Ironman/Honormode, but the most impactful one is probably "Hidden Alicia". In this mode, Alicia will be automated and inject mental changes without your control. This happens in a hidden way where you have no idea what she's currently up to. The mode is particularly intended for those want a more immersive experience for role playing Aura's corruption without her knowledge of what's happening to her and for those who didn't like the 2 player protagnist nature of the game and would rather focus on just one protagonist.

Since this mode has a big score multiplier it also doubles as a challenge mode for those who want to race Alicia so she can only make a minimum number of mental changes.

[h2]Community Translations[/h2]

Finally, we have been working on expanding our infrastucture so that we can support translations in the game. Sadly, since the game is very story-heavy, hiring dedicated translators isn't feasable. Based on my research, creating a translation into even a single language would require me to blow every USD I earned from the release. So instead I decided to go down the route of enabling community translations. If you are interested in participating, [url=https://discord.gg/hSrcVVSe]join us in the game's Discord [/url].

Aaaand that's most of what's new. There are some other things, such as improved reactivity for Aura in Chapter 3 where a lot of "I'm sorry, George" texts are now skipped to better reflect their change in relationship.

I hope the past gave you a decent overview of what's to come. For more details, check out my other social media channels.

notes.title: Release 1.0.2
notes.content:
Heyho!

Besides a bunch of bugfixes (hopefully fixing the last broken achievements), this patch mostly focuses on one major goal: Introducing a simple modding system.

When installing external mods to the game, Steam had kept reverting them when updating. I had hoped that I solved the issue in the 1.0.1 patch by improving the organization of the files that were prone to causing conflicts, but it appears that checksum mismatches alone can be enough to trigger steam reverting files and thus all "installed" mods.

The new mod loading system I have implemented over the week was originally planned for 1.1.0 as I don't want to implement high-risk features like that in patch releases and it's very likely I have overlooked something and will have to do a hotfix over the weekend - but its support for adding game modifications without overwriting old files should finally fix the problem of steam reverting mod installations for good.

I have also seen various players create their own changes to the game. If you would like to stop those from getting overwritten as well, check out the sample-mod in the mods/ folder to see how you can turn your own changes into a proper mod that can be persisted across updates!

notes.title: Hotfix 1.0.0b
notes.content:
Heyho!

Some people reported issues of game crashes when steam would try to trigger an achievement.

We were able to identify two possible cases where this can happen and fixed them - I hope that these fixes will cover the crashes for everyone who had them. The most common case seemed to be when starting the Game.exe from the steam folder instead of using the steam client. 

I hope we are doing everything 1000% the Steam way now, but due to my inexperience of creating working with the Steam API, I cannot promise that we covered all of our bases.

There is a second bugfix here for a potential lock that would prevent certain Earth scenes from triggering. But in the reporter used a cheated save and I wasn't able his issue on a test playthrough, so I don't think it's possible to replicate the state in an uncheated state. But if someone else did somehow manage to suffer the same issue, the implementation is more robust now.

notes.title: Release Date Fixed - 7th Feb
notes.content:
Beginning of the month, I pushed the release date back by one more week in order to give the game some more time for testing. As of yesterday, I released the beta build of the game and also locked in the final Steam release date: 

[h1][b]Feb 7th [/b] is the date![/h1]

I literally cannot change the date anymore in the steam UI, so from this point going forward, that's the definitve release date!

Furthermore, I also updated the demo to the new 1.0.0-beta-1 build. There is no important new content in it - however, a bunch of quality of life improvements, polish work and bugfixes made their way in. In particular, the World Fog feature, which puts a fog effect on parts of the world map which have not been unlocked, should help to avoid new players getting lost in the early game.

The remaining work on the game is now 99% more bugfix and polish work.
Let's hope the last two weeks until the release can give us more wishlists so we can break into New & Trending on release day!
